feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV with clear senior-level positioning, logical career progression, and credible experience in digital communications strategy. It reads professionally and is largely polished, but it would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear narrative of progression within one organization, showing increasing scope from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong relevance for digital strategy roles: web/CMS, analytics, governance, multimedia, and cross-channel communications are all well covered.  
- Good credibility through concrete platforms and scale indicators such as “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools like GA4, BigQuery, and Drupal.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact beyond scope: include outcomes like traffic growth, email engagement, production efficiency, cost savings, team size, or campaign results.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; this repetition weakens structure and makes the CV feel longer than necessary.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (basic working proficiency)” or similar.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the experience section, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it with sharper phrasing and one clearer differentiator would increase impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard CV style.
- Lead with seniority and scope: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience across web, email, social, multimedia, and platform modernization.”
- Add a stronger differentiator tied to recent work, such as enterprise web transformation, digital governance, or mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Simplify “building the workflows and systems that support complex, mission-driven organizations” to “designing scalable workflows and digital systems for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” closely overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” and “stakeholder coordination” are also repeated elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section is too broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the wording and emphasizing higher-value strategic capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, CV-specific terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS modernization,” and “Analytics, insights & optimization.”
- Prioritize senior-level, recent strengths over tactical tasks; e.g., lead with strategy, governance, platform modernization, and cross-functional leadership.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout; change “communication” to “communications” and consider “cross-functional” instead of “cross-department.”
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow automation & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming this section or using it only for broad themes not repeated elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also duplicates Soft Skills almost verbatim.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo roles below and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, recent strategic value, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or named initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise the National Association of Counties on enterprise digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, and cross-channel communications operations.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into one impact-focused line: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, modular microsites, and member-facing resource hubs, while providing front-end development and CMS troubleshooting.”
- Keep one systems/governance bullet: “Improved communications workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make AI search the signature bullet and quantify if possible: “Leading an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats the Director of Digital Media entry; emphasize advisory/consulting scope instead of rebuilding prior responsibilities.
- Microsite and AI search details duplicate Recent Projects; avoid naming both here unless you add measurable results.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be even stronger if the opening were tighter and more bullets showed outcomes, not just scope.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper impact summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading platform modernization and multi-channel audience growth.”
- Tighten and front-load the biggest achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible for channels/studio/analytics: subscriber growth, engagement rates, production volume, cost savings, reporting speed, or decision-making improvements.
- Consider a cleaner 4–5 bullet structure: website modernization; channel leadership; in-house studio buildout; analytics stack expansion; governance/operating model improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email/social/video leadership” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; emphasize enterprise ownership, modernization, budget, and systems here.
- Video buildout may overlap with older video-production bullets; frame this as scaling institutional capacity, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with sharper verbs and any measurable production or audience growth.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show build-out and impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance and content operations at scale
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider dropping “leadership” from one line to avoid repetition across bullets.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g. “Content operations for 10,000+ page, multi-publisher web environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep this section as a concise summary, not a repeat of experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. This topline item should emphasize the most marketable, recent platform strengths and group lower-priority tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Recast from a flat list into 3–4 grouped phrases focused on current value: “Drupal and CMS modernization,” “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery),” “API integrations and workflow automation,” “AI-enabled search and Airtable-based systems.”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages unless they are important targets for current roles; they are not strongly evidenced in recent experience.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based workflow systems” for clarity and stronger business relevance.
- Suggested rewrite: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based workflow systems • AI-enabled search experiences”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Platform/tool detail also overlaps with Technical + IT; keep this version higher-level.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make this more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than a software inventory.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Consider adding one higher-value phrase tied to recent work: “analytics infrastructure” or “measurement strategy” to align with the 2022–present roles.
- If space allows, replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” and “SEO and performance analysis” with “SEO, UX and conversion/performance analysis” for clearer scope.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and leave full tool detail below.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more senior, selective, and tied to the most recent/highest-impact multimedia capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, leadership-level phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ/multi-camera systems • Virtual event production”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better reflect the studio build and senior ownership shown in recent roles.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier: “Built and operated in-house studio workflows” or “Scaled in-house advocacy and event production.”
- Keep only 4–5 terms; remove lower-level wording like “editing” unless the target role is hands-on production focused.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “livestreaming”; combine to avoid padding.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add context on level of use or be tightened to emphasize the most relevant, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize current/recent platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add proficiency context instead of just names, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint/Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with senior-level positioning.
- If you want more impact, replace the weakest/least relevant platform with a qualifier tied to scope: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration)**, if formatting elsewhere supports brief parentheticals.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider keeping platforms in only one place.
- Drupal impact is already demonstrated strongly in recent experience, so avoid repeating long Drupal detail here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should emphasize implementation tools that support recent delivery, not repeat broad web skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope or outcomes in parentheses to show applied use, e.g. **Google Tag Manager (event tracking implementation)**, **GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)**, **Cloudflare Workers (edge scripting/performance)**.
- Consider dropping versioned labels like **HTML5/CSS3** unless older formatting is used elsewhere; **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- **Workflow automation** appears elsewhere; GitHub Actions may be better referenced there if not central to technical implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize systems you likely used strategically in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-value/general tools unless strongly used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to increase impact, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases), Power Automate/Zapier (cross-platform automations), Jira/Asana (project operations)**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; keep this item as a concise tool list, not a second skills summary.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, prioritize true automation/project systems over chat platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal enterprise email platform ownership rather than just tool familiarity.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If space allows, prioritize strongest/recent platform first based on actual hands-on use; keep to 3 tools max

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated email/channel leadership already covered in Work Experience; avoid adding generic claims like “managed newsletters” here.
- “Engagement” may be too broad unless supported elsewhere; consider “Email Marketing Platforms” if these tools were primarily used for email.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, with concrete outputs rather than leadership language that is better reserved for 2018–2024 roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-career buildout and production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital communications function supporting web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer scope/results if available: website refresh size, livestream/event volume, frequency/views of weekly video updates, or growth in output/capacity.
- Tighten the close to execution + light supervision: “Produced livestreams and recurring video updates, supported a major website refresh, and coordinated day-to-day work for a digital media associate.”
- Remove vague phrases like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” unless you can quantify the improvement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; frame this as launching or early production support.
- “guidance to a digital media associate” risks duplicating later management leadership; keep it modest.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it tighter and emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout outcome: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; if possible, replace with a specific output or audience/result.
- If you have metrics, add one: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast expanded member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item centered on innovation/research support + first podcast launch.
- Avoid repeating broad web/email/social responsibilities here since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
